core_obligations: Consider the family of all quasi-coherent O_X-submodules of G and form the image G' of their direct sum in F (proof lines 2827-2832).
Show that G' is quasi-coherent as a direct sum and an image of quasi-coherent modules, and that it is contained in G (proof lines 2832-2839).
For a quasi-coherent H and a map alpha : H -> G, show that the image of the composite H -> F is quasi-coherent, hence contained in G', so alpha factors through G' (proof lines 2841-2847).
Conclude the bijectivity of the displayed Hom map and the uniqueness of G' (proof lines 2847-2848).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a quasi-coherent O_X-module F on an algebraic space X and an O_X-submodule G of F, there is a unique quasi-coherent submodule G' contained in G that is universal for maps from quasi-coherent modules into G, hence the largest quasi-coherent submodule of G (source lines 2809-2824). The construction takes the indexed family of all quasi-coherent submodules contained in G, forms the image of their direct sum in F, and uses that direct sums, images and kernels of quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic space stay quasi-coherent; the universal property is verified by showing that the image of a map from a quasi-coherent module into G is quasi-coherent and hence among the family.
